turn_text: I also know that you've been a part of a discussion about moving to a biennial budget and there are a number of folks that are willing to have that conversation. Is there political will to do that? And if you can't get a single year deal, then what makes a two year deal any easier?

Well, what makes it easier is the fact that you take the election year politics out of it. If you look historically since 1974, on election years, 80 percent of those years we have no budget at all. The budget is one of the most difficult votes that any member of Congress takes because it focuses like a laser on what your priorities are and voters get to see it. But getting that two-year cycle taken care of One of the big benefits in our efforts to reduce federal spending is that every single agency has a use it or lose it mentality. And so for the last four or five weeks of the fiscal year, roughly 19% to 20% of all federal spending takes place then. And there's a spike of about $20 billion in the last week alone.
